correctness.rationale: Exact two-support-line linear-system formula gives the only pole at antipodal normals, with uniformly removable same-angle limit. Uniform Taylor and derivative expansions yield the width/angle pole and O(R^-2) probability remainder. The inverse-distance mark Jacobian yields density convergence and total variation. For constant width, curvature radii at antipodes sum to w, giving the exact nonnegative squared deficit; its zero set is precisely translated disks. Smooth threefold tanh-radius families satisfy width, positivity and closure and attain all intermediate coefficients while approaching zero. Standalone deterministic quadrature matches the exact circle tail and harmonic support curves for R=100,300,1000. Proof is analytic; finite tests are supplementary.

value.rationale: The naturally observed distance between two sampled supporting tangents gives a measurable geometric tail coefficient. Its exact stability identity distinguishes equal-perimeter, equal-width convex bodies, singles out disks sharply, and characterizes the complete possible range (including smooth near-zero examples). The marked law explains the rare antipodal geometry and gives a nontrivial size-biased direction sample. This is more than a routine circle benchmark or an arbitrary numerical invariant.
